metadata.title: Drew Ogletree sees one target in Week 1
metadata.description: Drew Ogletree failed to catch his only target in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree was one of many disappointing options in the Indianapolis offense in Week 1, with the tight end remaining best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree (neck) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Drew Ogletree is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree was a full participant in practice. He'll be good to go for Sunday's season opener.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Not limited Thursday
metadata.description: Ogletree (neck) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The tight end was limited by a neck injury a day earlier. Ogletree is trending toward playing in Sunday's opener against Baltimore. The 2022 sixth-round pick has added depth to the Colts' tight-end spot throughout his career, seeing action on special teams as well.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Ogletree (neck) was limited at Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: The Colts will play the Ravens to begin the season, though it's unknown if Ogletree will be on the field for that contest. The 28-year-old has spent his entire career with the Colts, most recently amassing four catches for 27 yards and one touchdown in 15 regular-season games during the 2025 campaign. While Ogletree isn't expected to see much attention from Daniel Jones in Week 1, his absence could mean an extra target or two for Mo Alie-Cox.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Re-ups with Colts for one year
metadata.description: Ogletree (neck) re-signed with the Colts on a one-year contract Friday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree has recovered from a neck injury that landed him on injured reserve to finish the 2025 season. He's expected to continue filling a depth role and contributing primarily as a blocker after recording 22 catches for 283 yards and four touchdowns across 44 appearances over the past three regular seasons with Indianapolis.

metadata.title: Colts Re-Sign Drew Ogletree to One-Year Deal
metadata.description: The Indianapolis Colts re-signed tight end Drew Ogletree to an undisclosed one-year deal on Friday, league sources told James Boyd of The Athletic. The former sixth-round pick in 2022 out of Youngstown State missed his entire rookie season due to a torn ACL in his knee. Since then, he has had four touchdown catches in three years and has mostly been used as a blocker on offense. Ogletree has a total of 22 catches for 283 yards and four touchdowns on 41 targets in his three seasons played in Indianapolis. Last year was his worst stat-wise, as the 27-year-old caught just four passes on six targets for 27 yards and one touchdown in 15 games (five starts). Ogletree isn't even a stash option in dynasty/keeper leagues and could be the TE4 for the Colts going into next season, behind Tyler Warren, Will Mallory, and Sean McKeon.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Ends 2025 on IR
metadata.description: Ogletree finished his 2025 campaign with four receptions for 27 yards and one touchdown. The tight end suffered a neck injury in Week 17 against the 49ers that ended his season.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree was a pivotal special-teams player for the Colts, logging 68 percent of snaps or better in every contest he played in until he suffered his neck injury. The 2022 sixth-round pick's injury came at an unfortunate time in his career, as the 27-year-old will enter 2026 as an unrestricted free agent coming off an injury.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Lands on IR
metadata.description: The Colts placed Ogletree (neck) on injured reserve Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree will miss at least Indianapolis' next four games due to a neck injury suffered during the team's Week 16 loss to San Francisco. If the Colts manage to somehow get into the playoffs and make a deep playoff run, the depth tight end could be a candidate to retake the field late January, though the Colts' chances of making the postseason are quite slim.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Out for Sunday
metadata.description: Ogletree (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Jaguars, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
metadata.analysis: The Youngstown State product opened the Colts' week of practice with consecutive DNPs after sustaining a neck injury in the Week 16 loss to the 49ers, so it's no surprise that he won't play Sunday. Ogletree has appeared in 15 games this season, catching four of six targets for 27 yards and a touchdown. Expect Will Mallory to operate as Indianapolis' No. 3 tight end in Ogletree's stead in Week 17.

metadata.title: Drew Ogletree - Listed as DNP to open Week 17 prep
metadata.description: The Colts listed Ogletree (neck) as a DNP on Wednesday's estimated practice report.
metadata.analysis: Ogletree sustained a neck injury during the Colts' loss to the 49ers on Sunday. The injury prevented him from participating in Wednesday's walkthrough, and the fourth-year tight end will have two more opportunities to return to practice ahead of Sunday's home game against the Jaguars.
